Induce protein expression by adding 500 μL of 1 M IPTG (final concentration 0.5 mM) and incubate at 18 °C shaking at 200 rpm in a shaking incubator overnight. Pellet the bacteria at 4,000 rpm for 15 min and discard the medium. Resuspend the bacteria pellet in 50 mL of lysis buffer 1 and directly place in a -20 °C freezer for at least one day to break the cells. This is an optional step; the aim is to break the bacteria through gradual ice crystal formation. Thaw the bacteria pellets in ice-cold water and sonicate the pellet on ice at maximum amplitude of 20 μm for 40 s, interval 60 s. Repeat 5–10 times until the cell lysate becomes less viscous. Pellet cell debris using the Ti 45 rotor at 25,000× g at 4 °C for 30 min. Collect supernatant and add 4 mL of Glutathione Sepharose ® 4B slurry (i.e., 2 mL of Glutathione Sepharose ® 4B beads). Incubate rolling at 4 °C for 90 min. Pellet the beads at 500× g for 3 min at 4 °C. Wash the beads with wash buffer five times. Resuspend the beads in 10 mL of wash buffer, add 200 μL of GST-3C (5 mg/mL, obtained from Crick Structural Biology Platform), and incubate rolling at 4 °C overnight. GST-3C protease is also commercially available, and can be purchased from Merck (PreScission Protease, catalog number: GE27-0843-01). Check the protein purity by SDS-PAGE, collect the peak fraction, and concentrate the protein using a Vivaspin 20 concentrator column (MWCO 10K). Final stock protein concentration is usually ~6 mg/mL. steps.title: Express and purify ATG3 from E. coli
steps.instruction: Transform pGEX6P1‑GST‑3C‑ATG3 into BL21 (DE3) cells, plate on LB agar with 100 µg/mL ampicillin and incubate 37 °C overnight. Inoculate a single colony into 120 mL LB + 100 µg/mL ampicillin in a 250 mL flask and grow 37 °C, 180 rpm overnight. Dilute 25–30 mL of this culture into 1 L LB + 100 µg/mL ampicillin in a 2 L flask (OD₆₀₀≈0.1); repeat to obtain a total of 4 L. Grow 3–5 h at 37 °C, 200 rpm until OD₆₀₀≈0.8. Induce with 500 µL 1 M IPTG (final 0.5 mM) and incubate 18 °C, 200 rpm overnight. Pellet cells at 4 000 rpm, 15 min, discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 50 mL Lysis buffer 1 and freeze at –20 °C for ≥1 day (optional). Thaw on ice, sonicate on ice at max amplitude 20 µm for 40 s with 60 s pause, repeat 5–10 times until lysate is less viscous. Centrifuge at 25 000×g, 4 °C, 30 min (Ti 45 rotor). Add 4 mL Glutathione‑Sepharose 4B slurry (equivalent to 2 mL beads) to the supernatant, roll 4 °C for 90 min. Pellet beads at 500×g, 3 min, 4 °C. Wash beads five times with Wash buffer. Resuspend beads in 10 mL Wash buffer, add 200 µL GST‑3C protease (5 mg/mL) and roll 4 °C overnight. Collect eluate and concentrate with a Vivaspin 20 (MWCO 10 kDa) to 1–2 mL. Perform size‑exclusion chromatography on a Superdex 200 16/60 GL column equilibrated in Equilibration buffer. Assess purity by SDS‑PAGE, pool peak fractions and reconcentrate with Vivaspin 20 to ~6 mg/mL. Flash‑freeze aliquots in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Express and purify LC3B S3C from E. coli
steps.instruction: Transform pAL‑GST‑3C‑LC3B (1‑120) S3C into BL21 (DE3) cells, plate on LB agar with 50 µg/mL kanamycin and incubate 37 °C overnight. Inoculate a single colony into 120 mL LB + 50 µg/mL kanamycin in a 250 mL flask and grow 37 °C, 180 rpm overnight. Dilute 25–30 mL of this culture into 1 L LB + 50 µg/mL kanamycin in a 2 L flask (OD₆₀₀≈0.1); repeat to obtain 4 L total. Grow 3–5 h at 37 °C, 200 rpm until OD₆₀₀≈0.8. Induce with 500 µL 1 M IPTG (final 0.5 mM) and incubate 18 °C, 200 rpm overnight. Pellet cells at 4 000 rpm, 15 min, discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 50 mL Lysis buffer 1 and freeze at –20 °C for ≥1 day (optional). Then follow the same purification steps as for ATG3 from sonication onward (steps 1e–1l), yielding a final stock of ~7 mg/mL. Flash‑freeze aliquots in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Express and purify ATG7 from Sf9 cells
steps.instruction: Sterilize the transfer plasmid pBacPAK‑His₃‑GST‑ATG7 by filtering through a 0.2 µm centrifugal filter. Seed 0.5 × 10⁶ Sf9 cells per well in a 6‑well plate and incubate static at 27 °C for ≥1 h. Prepare transfection mix: combine 0.5 µg plasmid, 50 ng flashBAC GOLD DNA, and 200 µL Sf‑900 II SFM medium; add 2 µL Fugene HD and incubate room temperature 20 min. Add 800 µL Sf‑900 II SFM to the mix, aspirate medium from the cells and add ~1 mL transfection mixture onto the cells; incubate static 27 °C overnight. Add another 1 mL Sf‑900 II SFM containing gentamicin 10 µg/mL and amphotericin B 0.25 µg/mL; incubate 4 days static at 27 °C. Harvest cells and supernatant, add 1.5 mL of this mixture to 50 mL Sf9 cells at 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL; shake 27 °C, 140 rpm for 3 days. Collect supernatant (baculovirus) and use to infect 400 mL Sf9 culture (1.5 × 10⁶ cells/mL) with 1 mL virus; shake 27 °C, 140 rpm for 60 h. Harvest cells by centrifugation 600×g, 10 min, 4 °C and freeze at –80 °C. Thaw pellet on ice, resuspend in 30 mL Lysis buffer 2 and sonicate on ice at 50 % amplitude for 10 s with 60 s pause, repeat 3–5 times. Centrifuge at 30 000×g, 4 °C, 30 min (Ti 45 rotor). Add 2 mL Glutathione‑Sepharose 4B slurry (1 mL beads) to supernatant, roll 4 °C for 90 min. Pellet beads 500×g, 3 min, 4 °C; wash five times with Wash buffer. Resuspend beads in 5 mL Wash buffer, add 100 µL GST‑3C (5 mg/mL) and roll 4 °C overnight. Concentrate eluate with a Vivaspin 6 (MWCO 30 kDa) to 300–500 µL. Perform SEC on a Superdex 200 10/300 GL column equilibrated in Equilibration buffer. Verify purity by SDS‑PAGE, pool peak fractions and reconcentrate with Vivaspin 6 to ~2 mg/mL. Flash‑freeze aliquots in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Label LC3B S3C with IANBD fluorophore
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 mM IANBD‑amide stock in DMSO and store at –20 °C for long‑term use. Equilibrate a PD Minitrap G‑25 column with 8 mL Labelling buffer. Apply 250 µL of 5 mg/mL LC3B S3C to the column, collect the eluate (buffer exchange). Re‑measure protein concentration and prepare 400 µL of ~100 µM LC3B S3C; add 100 µL of 10 mM IANBD‑amide. Incubate 1 h at room temperature in the dark. Quench by adding 20 µL of 100 mM L‑cysteine. Equilibrate a second PD Minitrap G‑25 column with 8 mL Assay buffer. Apply ~500 µL of the reaction mixture, collect eluate to remove excess dye. Determine protein concentration by Bradford assay and confirm labeling by SDS‑PAGE (unreacted dye appears as a front). Mix 125 µL glycerol with 500 µL NBD‑labelled LC3B S3C to obtain a final glycerol concentration of 20 % (v/v). Aliquot, flash‑freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 2 mM POPC/DOPE liposomes
steps.instruction: Mix POPC and DOPE lipids at a 50:50 mol % ratio. Dry the lipid mixture under nitrogen gas for 5 min, then place in an Eppendorf Concentrator for 2 h to remove residual solvent. Add 1 mL Assay buffer to the dried film and vortex until fully resuspended. Perform five freeze‑thaw cycles by alternating liquid nitrogen immersion and a 42 °C water bath until the suspension is completely thawed. Extrude the liposome suspension using a Mini‑Extruder: first pass the solution 21 times through a 0.2 µm polycarbonate membrane, then pass it at least 41 times through a 0.1 µm membrane. Verify vesicle size with a Zetasizer Nano ZS; if the polydispersity index (PDI) exceeds 0.2, repeat extrusion through the 0.1 µm membrane. Store liposomes at 4 °C and use within two days.

steps.title: Assemble real‑time ATG8 lipidation reaction
steps.instruction: In a low‑binding tube, combine the following to a final volume of 78.4 µL: 0.8 µL ATG7 stock (20 µM, gives 0.2 µM final), 0.8 µL ATG3 stock (20 µM, 0.2 µM final), 0.2 µL E3 complex stock (20 µM, 0.05 µM final), 40 µL Liposome stock (2 mM, 0.05 µM final), 1.6 µL NBD‑labelled LC3B S3C stock (1 µM, 0.05 µM final), and 35 µL Assay buffer. For control reactions, replace the omitted component with an equal volume of Assay buffer. Transfer the 78.4 µL mixture into a 10 mm path‑length quartz cuvette (capacity ≥100 µL).

steps.title: Record NBD fluorescence kinetics
steps.instruction: Place the cuvette in an FP‑8300 spectrofluorometer set to 37 °C. Configure excitation at 468 nm (bandwidth 5 nm) and emission at 535 nm (bandwidth 10 nm). Program a total measurement time of 20 min with two intervals: Interval 1 (0–80 s) – record fluorescence every 20 s (equilibration phase); Interval 2 (80–1 200 s) – record fluorescence every 10 s (reaction phase). Start the acquisition. At the end of Interval 1 (between 60 and 80 s), add 1.6 µL of 50 mM MgATP (final concentration 1 mM) and mix gently. Continue recording for the remainder of the run. Repeat the entire measurement for each experimental condition (no ATG7, no ATG3, no E3, no liposomes, no ATP, and complete reaction). For the “no ATP” condition, add 1.6 µL Assay buffer instead of MgATP.
